_about: How each kind of enemy fights in the rebuilt fight (rule 63b: 'Battle Brothers has its AI for the enemies correctly'; every archetype's behaviour from the library as data, before any skin). A behaviour is a set of switches the fight's one AI reads; each row quotes the wiki page (or Paolo's rule) it comes from. No number here is felt: the numbers they use (reach, hit chance, AP) are the rules' and the weapons'.

brigand_thug.quote: In the early game Brigand groups usually consist of [[Brigand Thug|Thugs]] and sometimes [[Brigand Raider|Raiders]].

lower_brigand_raider.quote: If armed with a long weapon like Pike and there are no enemies nearby, they wait to not get ahead of their melee allies.

brigand_raider.quote: If armed with a long weapon like Pike and there are no enemies nearby, they wait to not get ahead of their melee allies.

lower_brigand_marksman.quote: Their backline usually consists of [[Brigand Marksman|Marksmen]] who give Brigands ranged superiority, and if they think they have it, they will stand their ground and shoot at you.

brigand_marksman.quote: Their backline usually consists of [[Brigand Marksman|Marksmen]] who give Brigands ranged superiority, and if they think they have it, they will stand their ground and shoot at you.

brigand_poacher.quote: Their backline usually consists of [[Brigand Marksman|Marksmen]] who give Brigands ranged superiority

wiederganger.quote: They don't have any idea about careful approach and instead slowly walk towards you

direwolf.quote: Direwolves rush you even if they will have no AP left to attack.

brigand_marauder.quote: Brigand Marauders start appearing in the middle game, one or more among weaker brigands.

brigand_leader.quote: The Leader spawns in the very back and usually does not hurry to enter battle.

geist.quote: Geists sometimes accompany zombies. They usually try to stay behind them, screaming at your squad from a few tiles of distance. If your resolve if very high, they give up and instead fight in melee, using their touch.

necromancer.quote: Necromancers stay far behind their undead minions and cast spells from there. There is rarely more than one of them.

armored_wiederganger.quote: slowly walk towards you (the Wiederganger's walk, armoured)

goblin_skirmisher.quote: Skirmishers like to use throwing weapons and nets, and will Footwork often, sometimes even into worse position.

lower_goblin_skirmisher.quote: Skirmishers like to use throwing weapons and nets, and will Footwork often, sometimes even into worse position.

goblin_wolfrider.quote: Goblin Wolfrider is a fast enemy from the Goblins faction.

orc_warrior.quote: Orc Warriors are slow and heavy. They have the ability to disrupt formations and they use it mostly to get close to vulnerable backliners or to claim the high ground.

lower_orc_warrior.quote: Orc Warriors are slow and heavy. They have the ability to disrupt formations and they use it mostly to get close to vulnerable backliners or to claim the high ground.

orc_young.quote: Orc Young (the young of the orcs' line: Charge, the Orc Hand-to-Hand Attack)

brigand_leader_champion.quote: Champions are stronger versions of enemies that always have a named item
brigand_leader_champion.why: DIFFICULTY [the curve] 11/3: a champion fights as the kind he is a stronger version of (the brigand leader's brain)

goblin_skirmisher_champion.quote: Champions are stronger versions of enemies that always have a named item
goblin_skirmisher_champion.why: DIFFICULTY [the curve] 11/3: a champion fights as the kind he is a stronger version of (the skirmisher's brain, KID)

orc_warrior_champion.quote: Champions are stronger versions of enemies that always have a named item
orc_warrior_champion.why: DIFFICULTY [the curve] 11/3: a champion fights as the kind he is a stronger version of (the orc warrior's brain, HEAVY)

line.quote: However, Brigands are often too undisciplined to maintain formation. Some of them can run towards you even when they have ranged superiority.

backline.quote: if they think they have it, they will stand their ground and shoot at you

soft.quote: Being a ranged units, they can target anyone they want and prefer to shoot at shieldless units or rookies
soft.also: COMBAT [the enemy plays its part] (coordinator): 'pick the unarmoured head'
soft.how: a shot's worth is multiplied by one plus how soft the man is: no car door, a rookie (level 1), a bare head

walker.quote: slowly walk towards you, getting hit by [[Spears|spearwalls]]

rusher.source: VAMILY.md rule 63b (and bb_all/0629_Direwolf.txt: they rush you)
rusher.quote: wolves run round the back for the weakest

crew.quote: A typical battle starts with both parties in a line formation (1-2 lines deep for your forces, may be deeper for the enemy), with at least 5 hexes between parties.
crew.why: the crew keeps the line it starts in and lets the undisciplined brigands come (VAMILY rule 63b: 'the driver gate fields 12 against a crew that behaves'); it walks forward only when no foe is coming

auto._about: Rule 70b (Paolo 10/4: 'the Auto button, we are far from complete'): AUTO plays your men the way Battle Brothers' AI plays its own, formation held. Each switch the crew brain reads, with the page it comes from.

high_ground.quote: It is always advantageous to have the high ground in any battle and the AI will try to occupy the high ground whenever possible, especially their ranged units.
high_ground.how: a tile on a roof scores the rules' own height bonus per level over flat; a shooter weighs it twice

spread_attacks.quote: The AI will not stack all its attacks on the weakest target as this would be unfair and really hard to counter.
spread_attacks.how: a target's worth is divided by one plus the number of times your men already swung at him this round

keep_formation.quote: all enemies will benefit from better positioning and better coordination amongst their ranks.
keep_formation.how: a man walking toward the fight never ends more than the line's depth ahead of the middle of his own line, and prefers a tile with a friend beside him (ours.formation_depth_lines)

shield_the_backline.quote: They'll be better at protecting their vulnerable units
shield_the_backline.also: bb_all/1145_Late Game Builds.txt: 'they must not be left unprotected for highly mobile melee units will slay them without difficulty'
shield_the_backline.how: a shooter never steps level with or ahead of the front man of his own melee line while that line stands

sees_only.quote: the AI can not target anyone it can not see.
sees_only.how: a man picks only targets his side can see

finds_a_shot.source: VAMILY.md rule 322 (Paolo 11/2); Battle Brothers' ai_engage_ranged (selectBestTargetTile: its max range, line of fire, a visible tile, and the PotentialDanger list; gist.github.com/Suor/82489e82556a81d51445bcd4717b3950)
finds_a_shot.quote: with auto combat you want the characters to get into places where they have the ability to hit the enemy... my sniper... ends his turn without trying to get to the best point of view, a place with line of sight where he can shoot
finds_a_shot.how: a shooter of his with no shot where he stands walks to the best tile that gives one: a shot this turn first, else a shot next turn; the order and the weights are ours.auto_finds_a_shot

best_turn.source: VAMILY.md rule 332 (Paolo 11/2); Battle Brothers' AI picks its best action and tile one turn at a time (ai_engage_ranged's PotentialDanger, gist.github.com/Suor/82489e82556a81d51445bcd4717b3950)
best_turn.quote: the best course of action in that turn, to do the most damage and take the least damage within that turn
best_turn.how: every action he can take this turn (a blow, a sweep, a perk, a swap and its blow, a walk and a blow, a reload, the squeeze, holding) scored as the hurt it deals minus the hurt he takes before his next turn where he ends; the best is taken; no multi-turn plans; out of breath he holds (the rest); the weights are ours.auto_best_turn

head.quote: One of tactics against them is sniping. You need a few archers with Bullseye, who are deployed in frontline, then move forward and shoot.
head.why: COMBAT [bestiary] 10/24: the company's brain (and AUTO) puts its blow on the MECHANIC whenever it can reach him, before any machine: the lesson the player meets is the one his own men show him

raider.quote: If armed with a long weapon like Pike and there are no enemies nearby, they wait to not get ahead of their melee allies.
raider.why: a raider flanks like the line (surround: he goes for the man his friends already hold); with a two-tile weapon he never walks out ahead of the one-tile men

leader.quote: The Leader spawns in the very back and usually does not hurry to enter battle.
leader.also: bb_all/0343_Captain.txt: 'Captain is an aura that increases the Resolve of other allies by +15% (range of 5 tiles)' (ours.captain_aura)
leader.how: before the lines meet he does not move; after, he never steps ahead of his own front man, so his aura stays over his line

screamer.quote: They usually try to stay behind them, screaming at your squad from a few tiles of distance. If your resolve if very high, they give up and instead fight in melee, using their touch.
screamer.why: COMBAT [ghosts and apparitions] 10/23 (rule 134): the scream from inside its reach, the touch when nobody in reach can still break

mechanic.quote: Necromancers stay far behind their undead minions and cast spells from there. ... Also they cast Raise Undead to bring an undead back to unlife with full HP. ... They can't cast spells if engaged in melee.
mechanic.why: COMBAT [bestiary] 10/24, THE MECHANIC (Paolo 9/29, his words in records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_BESTIARY_COUNT_9_29_26.md: 'a man who keeps reviving his robots; kill him and the machines drop'): he never walks ahead of his own front machine, reboots a fallen one whenever he can (twice a turn), shoots his pistol when nothing is down, and steps out of a man's reach to keep working

kid.quote: Skirmishers like to use throwing weapons and nets, and will Footwork often, sometimes even into worse position. ... They are fragile, but evasive. Their morale easily breaks.
kid.why: COMBAT [bestiary] 10/24, THE KIDS AND RUNNERS (records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_BESTIARY_COUNT_9_29_26.md: 'GOBLINS (kiting, nets, poison, wolf riders) -> KIDS AND RUNNERS on bikes and dirt quads with slings and nets'): the net on the man coming for them, the sling from range, and after the throw the step back out of reach (kiting)

rider.quote: Goblin Wolfrider is a fast enemy from the Goblins faction. (perks: Backstabber; action points 13)
rider.why: COMBAT [bestiary] 10/24: the runner on the dirt quad comes round the side for the man the others hold (the wolf's rush, the rider's Backstabber)

heavy.quote: They have the ability to disrupt formations and they use it mostly to get close to vulnerable backliners or to claim the high ground. They often end up surrounded after doing it.
heavy.why: COMBAT [bestiary] 10/24, THE HEAVY (records/BOHEMIA_BATTLE_BROTHERS_SCHOOL_THE_BESTIARY_COUNT_9_29_26.md: 'ORCS (mass, shove) -> THE HEAVY: exo-suit men, crash-bar shields, they push you off the tile'): he shoves the man in his way off the tile toward a shooter behind him, then walks into the hole

staff.quote: Is permanently dead if struck down and will not survive with a permanent injury.
staff.why: a camp follower never fights like the line (rule 470(a)): he moves himself, never by his hand, to the most defended tile his walk reaches (staff_ground: out of their reach, a fighter between him and every one of theirs, behind the line, a wall or a corner at his back, cover, high ground, huddled with the camp), away from any of theirs beside or behind him, never ending in their reach; the blade only when cornered; fleeing, he runs as any man. One beat a turn

hunt.value: an enemy that sees nobody walks the shortest open path toward your crew, never through a house
hunt.quote: Battle Brothers has its AI for the enemies correctly
hunt.why: measured on the frozen fight (V165): enemies who never see you hold forever and the fight never ends

avoid_surround.quote: Surrounding an opponent from multiple sides makes it easier to score a hit.
avoid_surround.why: every brain weighs a tile by friends beside it against foes beside it, so nobody walks alone into three men

camp_pull.source: records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_THE_STAFF_FIGHT_TOO_11_21_26.md C5 (VAMILY rule 468); bb_all/0657 Donkey: 'Enemies prefer attacking donkeys over your brothers'
camp_pull.quote: As the English were collecting prisoners, a band of French peasants led by local noblemen began plundering Henry's baggage behind the lines (Britannica, Agincourt)
camp_pull.why: a staff member's worth as a target, times his attacker's family's pull, ON TOP of what the fight already does (a blow already goes where it hurts most, and the marksman already prefers the soft: an unarmoured cook at level one is the softest thing on the board). Raiders and looters go for the baggage (x1.5: roaming crews, desert road crews, the lab's keepers, the kids). MEASURED (STAFF 11/21, the live fight headless, 8 of his with 3 staff against 6 to 9): at the research's draft (beasts x1.25, everyone else x1) a third to a half of the camp died every fight, most of it to the house's crossbows and to beasts; so soldiers (every other family) fight the company first (x0.5: they still take a staff member when he is the best hit in reach), and beasts x0.6 (at x1 54% of the camp died a beast fight, at x0.6 30%: still the family that kills the most of it). A man's family is the one whose factions (records/target/bb/roster.json families: in_the_fight and bb_factions, copied here and held equal by gates/the_staff_fight_too_gate.js) hold his own; two families, the bigger pull. walk_weight: a tile of theirs that reaches one of his staff is worth (pull - 1) x walk_weight x the hit cap more on their walk (only a pull over 1); hunt_steps: to their hunt his camp stands (pull - 1) x hunt_steps steps nearer than it is (x1.5: two steps), so raiders walk round his line for it. Draft, TUNING

raid.source: records/BOHEMIA_RESEARCH_THE_STAFF_FIGHT_TOO_11_21_26.md C5 step two (VAMILY rule 468); the Agincourt raid came from behind the line, Arsuf's enemy struck the separated baggage
raid.why: in a fight against raiders with staff on the board, one fight in five up to two of their men (never the leader, a boss, a champion, a beast or a machine) start on his back edge (the west side, and the north and south sides behind his line), more than turns_away turns' run from the nearest staff member, so no blow lands on the camp in their first turn; never on the game's first day (not_before_day); no tile that far, no raid. MEASURED (STAFF 11/21): the research's two turns' run (8 tiles) is never there: on the 20 by 15 board his camp stands 3 tiles from the west edge and 5 to 9 from the others. Draft, TUNING

guards_the_camp.why: AUTO guards the camp: a blow on a man of theirs who stands next to one of his staff is worth next_to_staff more to AUTO's pick; and a turn that ends beside one of his staff while a man of theirs is within threat_tiles of him, with no other fighter beside him yet, is worth beside more (AUTO's own units: a blow's expected harm, about 10 to 20). MEASURED (STAFF 11/21): x1.3/8 and x2/20 lost the same camp in the same 40 fights: the guard fires (165 blows, 119 turns in 8 fights) but the man who hits the cook is already AUTO's best blow; the camp is kept by where it stands and how it moves (archetypes.staff), so the numbers stay at the research's x1.3 with a turn beside worth 15. Draft, TUNING

staff_ground.source: VAMILY rule 470(a), Paolo 11/22: 'They're weak as fuck compared to the front line. They will stay behind. They will take defensive positions and they will attempt to not be flanked and circled.'; bb_all/0424 Combat Mechanics and bb_all/1316 Morale (the surround: +5% to hit for every attacker past the first; +3 resolve a man beside him)
staff_ground.why: how a camp follower weighs a tile (lower is safer; STAFF 11/22, slices/BOHEMIA_FIGHT.html __THEY_FIGHT_LIKE_STAFF__): danger a man of theirs who can reach it by their next turn; unscreened one of theirs with no fighter of his between him and the tile; foe_beside one of theirs on the tile's eight; foe_behind one of theirs west of him (his line faces east) within behind_tiles; open_side an open side of the eight (a wall, a building, cover or one of his own closes it: a corner is the best ground, nobody circles him there); cover_piece the board's cover beside the tile (ours.cover_defence); high_ground a roof; ahead_of_line a tile east of the middle of his standing fighters less behind_line_by; camp_beside another of the camp beside him (up to huddle_cap: they huddle); fighter_beside a fighter of his beside him; move_margin what a tile must beat where he stands by before he walks. Draft, TUNING

fear_run.source: VAMILY rule 482 on the staff as built (STAFF 2 11/26: 'a staff man running looks like fear'); records/BOHEMIA_STAFF_TWO_RULE_482_THE_STAFF_BETTER_11_26_26.md
fear_run.why: a camp person's walk on the glass only (the rules already moved him): a walk that starts within near tiles of one of theirs and takes him farther from the nearest is a scared run: his feet at keys a beat (the walk's own six keys twice as quick, every key drawn), the tiles in dur of a walk's time (never under half a beat, the floor a turn is seen at), his body leant lean of his height to the side he runs (none north or south), his cart upright and rattling. MEASURED (STAFF 2 11/26): 25% of camp walks in 20 AUTO fights are scared runs. Moved here from a constant in slices/BOHEMIA_FIGHT.html (STAFF 3 11/27, VAMILY rule 495(b): felt numbers in the one numbers table). Draft, TUNING
